newsitem.title: CANADA: Dylex to save C$1 million a year on changes.
newsitem.headline: Dylex to save C$1 million a year on changes.

text.p: Canada's largest apparel retailer, Dylex Ltd, will save C$1 million a year in costs after amalgamating the infrastructures of its two women's chains, said chief executive Elliott Wahle on Thursday.

The 73-store Fairweather chain and 62-outlet Braemar banner will consolidate their financing, marketing and human resources departments, among other backroom functions, Wahle told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Dylex will realize the savings starting in 1997.
Wahle added that "The banners will remain distinct."

Steven Somers, currently Fairweather's president, has been named to lead the two chains. Former Braemar president Joel Cooper resigned in May after Dylex stated its intention to sell Braemar but could not find a buyer. Dylex then bought Cooper's 25 percent stake, and now owns 100 percent.
Analysts applauded the move, saying it would help the retailer. Dylex posted second quarter earnings of C$0.01 a share on Thursday, down from a year-earlier C$0.03.
Retail analyst Len Kubas, president of Kubas Consultants, said "I think it makes sense to consolidate some of the expenses which are in common."
Another analyst, who declined to be identified, said "They're doing the right things: it'll bring the right result."
"I think the senior management team certainly knows what they're doing, in this situation," Kubas added.
Shares in the retailer gained 0.11 to hit 2.80 in moderate trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Thursday, nearing the year's high of 3.05.
Kubas said that in his 20-odd years of surveying the industry, clothing retailers have never seen such lacklustre demand as in the past few years.
This is forcing Dylex management to post poor results despite recent changes, Kubas said. "What's conspiring against them is this very difficult consumer environment."
Dylex underwent a restructuring after emerging from creditors' protection in early 1995, shedding 191 stores. Eventually new management took control out of the hands of the founding Posluns family.
Dylex also owns discount chain BiWay, upscale Club Monaco, menswear chains Harry Rosen and Tip Top Tailors as well as casual wear Thriftys. It has 730 outlets.
